Evidence-backed Compression itself is not the problem. WavLM fixed k=5 beats no downsampling by 0.89 WER points on test-clean while averaging 5h20m instead of 18h02m of A100 wall time per run (3.4× faster in this protocol). Phone-aligned pooling improves another 0.67 points at nearly the same kept ratio. The decoder benefits from a shorter prefix, but it also cares which frames are averaged together.
Inferred The current bottleneck is the path from char initialization to a stable task-aware policy. wav2vec2 reproduces the wav2vec2-derived char targets much more accurately than WavLM (0.893 vs. 0.799 CNN F1), while the boundary swap shows that later RL drift is more damaging than the initial imitation error. This motivates a candidate-boundary merge policy or an explicit char-retention constraint, not simply more epochs of the same unconstrained objective.

The clean-set compression gain survives three seeds. Fixed k=5 reaches 6.16±0.12 on test-clean versus 7.05±0.52 without downsampling, a 0.89-point gain with much smaller seed variance. It also reduces mean A100 wall time from 18h02m to 5h20m under the actual memory-safe protocols. Moderate mean-pooling can denoise redundant 50-Hz WavLM frames and regularize the Llama decoder by shortening its audio prefix. The effect is not universal, however: dev-clean is 6.08±0.12 versus 6.12±0.17, and test-other is 10.17±0.23 versus 10.10±0.40—both essentially tied. The no-downsampling memory protocol also changes batching and decode settings, so a fully matched no-downsampling control remains useful.
RL convergence is mixed, not complete in the task metric. Boundary rate and training reward stabilize, but only 4/18 runs select epoch 10; 13 select epochs 7–9 and 1 retain the pre-RL warm-up. Training reward often continues to improve after dev WER has peaked, and late-epoch WER frequently rebounds. The policy optimization has settled, but the reward/generalization alignment has not; simply training longer is unlikely to fix that without stronger early stopping or a better-aligned objective.
Alignment controls separate count from placement. Phone boundaries are the closest oracle to k=5 in cost (ρ=0.210 vs. 0.201) and improve WER from 6.16±0.12 to 5.49±0.23 clean and 10.17±0.23 to 9.21±0.33 other. Char boundaries retain more frames (ρ=0.293) but are stronger still at 5.03±0.42 / 8.07±0.43. Thus the fixed-rate gain combines smoothing with token-budget regularization, while another sizeable gain is available from content-aware placement. Learned policies should be compared to both k=5 and phone alignment, not only to no downsampling.

Evidence-backed The dual-encoder study isolates decoder initialization. With the exact same wav2vec2 detector, WavLM pooling, Bernoulli policy, rate band, and 10 RL epochs, the oracle-decoder start reaches 5.16±0.32 / 9.44±0.48 versus 6.48±0.14 / 10.04±0.15 from scratch. The gain is therefore not an encoder-capacity story; it is primarily a better decoder basin and shorter distribution-bridging problem.
Inferred The remaining test-other gap is boundary robustness. The hybrid oracle-init mean is only 0.13 points behind the three-seed char oracle on clean, but 1.37 points behind on other. No checkpoint-loading or frame-grid error was found. Harder acoustics appear to magnify small timing/coverage errors and the oracle-decoder distribution shift.

Evidence-backed WavLM is not a universal drop-in gain. It substantially improves the Transformer policy on test-other (for NLL co-training, 12.53→10.88), yet degrades the CNN NLL co-trained arm (6.19→6.93 clean; 11.12→12.01 other). Encoder quality interacts with the segmenter and decoder curriculum; quoting one encoder-wide ranking would hide that interaction.
Inferred Decoupling detection from pooling is promising. The char targets themselves come from wav2vec2, whose cold CNN F1 is 0.893 versus 0.799 with WavLM. Reusing the stronger wav2vec2 detector while pooling WavLM features recovers 5.16±0.32 / 9.44±0.48 with oracle decoder initialization. This separates boundary-timing compatibility from the representation presented to the LLM.

Evidence-backed The first-order dependency learns a sensible spacing prior, but converges early in task WER. Across the three long runs, best dev WER is 5.43±0.06 (epochs 1/2/4), improving 0.42 points over the 5.85 initialization. The latest available mean has rebounded to 6.04±0.11, while all transition gaps become negative. Extra constant-LR epochs strengthen the no-adjacent-boundary bias but overfit the decoder/policy pair.
Open question The current first-order AR gain is not yet replicated on held-out WER. The WavLM one-seed comparison is only −0.17 clean / −0.06 other, and 1/3 long wav2vec2 runs currently have both held-out files. Use the saved early best checkpoints; longer training under the same schedule is not evidence for convergence, and this result should not be conflated with the still-unimplemented full-prefix Transformer policy.

5 · Method — data, model & curriculum

Standard LibriSpeech ASR, but the audio-to-LLM interface is learned rather than fixed: a small per-frame policy decides where an utterance breaks into segments, so the compression rate can adapt to the audio instead of pooling every k frames by hand (the fixed-rate baseline this report compares against below).

Pipeline

The segmenter's predicted boundaries are the dynamic downsampling: more boundaries → more, shorter audio tokens reaching the decoder; fewer boundaries → a lower kept-ratio ρ and higher compression. Source for this figure: make_pipeline_figure.py (also emits an editable .drawio).

6 · Historical failure — collapse and the fix

Teacher-forced NLL from an undertrained decoder plus a per-frame entropy bonus drove the boundary probabilities to a uniform mush: the argmax produced ~0 boundaries, the decoder saw ~1 token, WER hit 100%.

Diagnosis. Entropy pushed every p→0.5 (the rate loss constrains only the sum, not sharpness) → uniform p, empty argmax. And teacher-forced NLL under-rewards audio → RL pushed ρ down. Fix: drop the entropy bonus + warm the decoder longer (2→6 epochs).

Kept-ratio ρ once RL turns on

collapsed → 0fixed: holds ~0.28RL start

x = epochs since RL begins (≤0 = warmup). Old run crashes to ρ≈0.005 in one RL epoch; fixed run holds ρ≈0.28. (Backbone also differs here — transformer vs CNN — see the analysis below for a same-backbone comparison.)

6b · Failure audit — two mechanisms, not one

Now that we have non-collapsing runs to compare against, it's worth being precise about the mechanism — the failure history is actually two different collapses, not one, and the eventual fix changed two variables at once, so this is an honest post-mortem rather than a clean ablation.

Failure #1 (original run): a true absorbing state, not entropy-smearing. At epoch 3 both the argmax ρ and the expected ρ crash together, to ≈0.003 and ≈0.002 — not to a moderate shared value. The instrumented GRPO trace (grpo_trace.py) makes the mechanism exact: for every traced utterance the collapsed policy has mean-p = 0.000 and per-frame entropy = 0.0000, so all K=8 sampled segmentations are bit-for-bit identical — same ρ, same reward, reward std = 0.0000, advantage = +0.000 for every sample. GRPO's group-relative advantage has zero within-group variance to learn from once every sample in the group is the same point — the gradient isn't small, it is exactly zero, everywhere. (Compare the healthy cold-start trace: mean-p 0.05–0.23, entropy 0.06–0.16, reward std 0.22–2.60, per-sample ρ spread up to 2×.) That's the absorbing state, and it explains why ρ stayed pinned at exactly 1.90e-3 for epochs 4 through 10 with no further movement.

Failure #2: argmax dies, expected survives

run (rate mode)epochargmax ρexpected ρ
jointB (cap+tax+floor)30.0050.184
jointB (cap+tax+floor)50.0020.077
jointC (band [0.1,0.3])30.0090.273
jointC (band [0.1,0.3])40.0030.218

Both CNN, entropy still on (floor 0.05→0.01). Expected ρ stays healthy — the floor/band mechanism works — while argmax ρ still collapses.

Failure #2 (A/B/C retry): a different collapse, caused by entropy, not the rate objective. Adding a floor (jointB) or a free band (jointC) worked exactly as designed — the expected ρ (Σp/T, the differentiable proxy) never crashes to zero, it stays right where the rate objective wants it. But the argmax ρ — what the decoder actually receives — collapses anyway, within one or two epochs, in both rate objectives (a soft floor and a hard free-band are structurally different, yet produce the identical divergence signature). That commonality points at the one thing neither rate objective constrains: sharpness. Per-frame Bernoulli entropy is maximized at p=0.5, and the entropy bonus (still on here) pushes every frame toward it; the rate loss only constrains the sum Σp, never the shape of the per-frame distribution. So the policy can satisfy "correct average rate" while every single frame sits uniformly below the argmax threshold (p>0.5) — expected count healthy, decoded count empty. (jointA, a two-sided pin — in principle the most collapse-resistant of the three — was killed mid-epoch-3 once the same pattern was already clear in its siblings, so we don't have its numbers, but nothing in the mechanism above is specific to jointB or jointC's rate objective.)
A separate, third observation: the reward pointed the wrong way. Within jointB's own run, as expected ρ fell 0.184→0.119→0.077 across epochs 3–5, the teacher-forced NLL reward improved (−3.01→−2.93→−2.84) — the gradient the segmenter received was actively rewarding fewer audio tokens. Consistent with an undertrained (2-epoch) decoder leaning on its text prior rather than the audio: noisy under-trained audio conditioning hurts more than it helps. This is a genuinely separate problem from the entropy/sharpness mechanism above — it's about the sign of the gradient, not its shape.

So which fix mattered? The runs that finally didn't collapse (nll_frozen/nll_mt/cer_mt) changed two things at once — dropped entropy to exactly 0 and extended warmup 2→6 epochs — so this isn't a controlled experiment and we can't say with certainty which was necessary. Our read of the evidence: dropping entropy is the better-supported primary fix for the argmax-collapse specifically — it's a direct, within-run, mechanism-level explanation (p→0.5 is a plain mathematical property of the entropy bonus, not something that depends on decoder quality) that reproduces identically across two structurally different rate objectives. The longer warmup targets the separate reward-misdirection problem above, and plausibly also helps sharpness indirectly — a better-trained decoder should give higher-SNR, more decisive per-frame reward gradients that can outcompete entropy's smoothing pull — but no run isolates "entropy-off/short-warmup" or "entropy-on/long-warmup", so that half of the story is inferred, not proven.

cer_mt_opt (2026-08-04): joint RL never beat its own warmup. Valid loss/WER at the end of warmup (epoch 6, segmenter still frozen) were 0.198 / 6.34% — better than every subsequent joint epoch (valid WER 10.17 → 10.98 → 7.50 → 10.30, noisy and non-monotonic through epochs 7–10). The checkpointer (min valid loss) correctly kept epoch 6, so the cer_mt_opt row above is the pre-RL warmup checkpoint re-evaluated, not a converged CER-reward result — contrast nll_mt, whose joint phase improved valid WER almost every epoch over the identical 4-epoch budget (6.53 → 6.29 → 6.03 → 5.62, ticking back up slightly to 5.78 at epoch 10). The blue curves above show a likely reason: train ρ_std during cer_mt_opt's joint phase (0.079–0.083) runs roughly double nll_mt's (0.037–0.040) — the free-running CER reward (K genuinely different decoded hypotheses per step) is a visibly noisier training signal than teacher-forced NLL, and 4 epochs wasn't enough for it to settle. The later corrected on-policy sweep resolves this: CNN CER genuinely trains to 6.67±0.41 / 11.31±0.39 WER, but still trails NLL co-training and costs about 3× more.
Completed Transformer result · stable training, negative backbone result. The best Transformer arm is NLL co-training at 7.16±0.37 clean / 12.53±0.81 other, versus CNN's 6.19±0.58 / 11.12±0.44 at a similar keep ratio (0.272 vs 0.265 on test-clean). Transformer CER selected epoch 7 in all three seeds and degraded afterward; the model trained, but it did not beat the smaller CNN boundary policy.

Appendix · architecture & trainable parameters

Exact counts for the wav2vec2-base configuration from the real modules (not estimates) — see segmenter.py and the hparams yaml. WavLM-Large uses 1024-d inputs with the same topology, so its input projections have different parameter counts.
